headerBody: Portugal: Tourist Scams documents 65 specific scams across Lisbon, Porto, Sintra and seven more cities, each verified against Portuguese police (PSP, GNR), the food-and-economic-safety authority ASAE, the consumer association DECO PROTESTE, Parques de Sintra, and real traveler reports on r/portugal and r/Lisbon. Every entry gives the exact script, the tells that expose it, and the Portuguese phrase that ends the encounter — including your legal right under 'não pedi, não pago' to refuse unordered restaurant couvert.
quadHead: Four ways Portugal catches tourists off guard.

quad.title: The Couvert You Never Ordered
quad.tl: You sit down and bread, olives, cheese and pâté arrive unasked — each €2–€6, landing €15–€35 on the bill before you've ordered a dish. Portuguese law lets you hand it back.

quad.title: The Tuk-Tuk 'Full City Tour'
quad.tl: A Ribeira tout quotes €80–€180 for a 'we'll show you everything' loop that's a 3–4 km walk — then routes you through port houses and shops that kick back 10–25%.

quad.title: The Fake Dealer & Fake Police
quad.tl: A man offers cheap 'hashish' (it's soap or oregano) near Rossio — then an accomplice flashing a 'police' badge demands a €100–€300 'fine' if you engaged.

quad.title: The 'Private VIP' Port Tasting
quad.tl: A 'personalized private tasting' is sold at €150–€250 a head — the same Gaia cellar pours the identical wines on its standard tour for €15–€35. The gap is pure commission.

body: Portugal: Tourist Scams is part of the tabiji.ai Travel Safety Series. Every scam is documented against Portuguese sources — PSP and GNR advisories, the food-and-economic-safety authority ASAE, the consumer association DECO PROTESTE, Parques de Sintra ticketing notices, and real traveler reports on r/portugal and r/Lisbon — not recycled from generic listicles.

65 specific scams across Lisbon, Porto, Sintra, Cascais, Coimbra, Faro, Funchal, Albufeira, Lagos and Nazaré. The exact scripts, the tells that give each one away, and the Portuguese phrases that shut it down — written in plain spelling you can show on your phone, including your 'não pedi, não pago' right to refuse unordered couvert.
Scams evolve, so the book is re-researched every year, and the current edition sits in your Kindle library. Built for the traveler who wants to move through Portugal relaxed, not braced.
